- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak or adjust downward 1–2 days after spike.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and model continues rising, reduce forecast slope; expect mean reversion within 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong downward correction after a forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 2–3 days post-peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag in direction change; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast variance by 15–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.3) and model still forecasts upward, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days; expect reversal.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but price is trending down; adjust forecast downward 1–2% for 2–3 days if sentiment >0.7 and price drops.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For sentiment >0.7 and price >75, model tends to overestimate; cap forecast at 75–78 for 3–5 days unless sentiment drops.
